title: How to Clean a Smelly Dishwasher

seo.title: How to Clean a Smelly Dishwasher
seo.meta_description: A smelly dishwasher usually has food debris in the filter, standing water, dirty seals, or a drainage problem.
seo.search_intent: Use a practical, safe method to clean a Smelly Dishwasher, with clear checks, limits, and next steps.

excerpt: A smelly dishwasher usually has food debris in the filter, standing water, dirty seals, or a drainage problem. Effective cleaning means removing the physical source of the odor before running an empty cleaning cycle with a manufacturer-approved product.
content_html:
A smelly dishwasher usually has food debris in the filter, standing water, dirty seals, or a drainage problem. Effective cleaning means removing the physical source of the odor before running an empty cleaning cycle with a manufacturer-approved product.

Clean the filter and remove visible debris

Turn the appliance off as directed, remove the user-accessible filter, and clear debris from the sump, spray arms, and door area. Do not reach blindly into areas that may contain broken glass or sharp fragments.

Clean door seals and the lower door edge

Grease and debris can collect where spray does not reach directly. Use a cloth and compatible cleaner, paying attention to folds without pulling or cutting the gasket.

Check whether water remains after the cycle

A small amount in the sump may be normal for some models, but dirty water covering the tub floor points to a drainage problem. Check the filter, accessible hose, and drain connection before trying to mask the odor.

Run a cleaning cycle only with compatible products

Use the cleaner or procedure specified by the manufacturer and never mix bleach with acids, vinegar, or other products. If odor returns quickly, investigate drainage, sink connection, or standing water rather than repeating chemical cycles.
